theorem Dense.continuous_sup {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α]
    [ConditionallyCompleteLattice α] [ClosedIicTopology α] {f : γ → α} [TopologicalSpace γ]
    {S : Set γ} (hS : Dense S) (hf : Continuous f) (h : BddAbove (f '' S)) :
    ⨆ i, f i = ⨆ s : S, f s := by
  rw [← sSup_range, ← sSup_range]
  obtain (_ | _) := isEmpty_or_nonempty γ
  · simp [Set.range_eq_empty]
  rcases h with ⟨a, ha⟩
  have hRange : BddAbove (range f) := ⟨a, by simpa [hS.continuous_upperBounds hf] using ha⟩
  have hImage : BddAbove (f '' S) := ⟨a, ha⟩
  refine (isLUB_csSup (range_nonempty f) hRange).unique ?_
  refine (isLUB_congr (hS.continuous_upperBounds hf)).mp (isLUB_ciSup_set hImage hS.nonempty)

requested_change: Change the hypothesis `h : BddAbove (range f)` to `h : BddAbove (f '' S)` (equivalently `BddAbove (range fun s : S => f s)`), keeping the conclusion and proof structure the same.

theorem Dense.continuous_sup' {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α]
    [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] [ClosedIicTopology α] {f : γ → α} [TopologicalSpace γ]
    {S : Set γ} (hS : Dense S) (hf : Continuous f) :
    ⨆ i, f i = ⨆ s : S, f s := by
  rw [← sSup_range, ← sSup_range]
  obtain (_ | _) := isEmpty_or_nonempty γ
  · simp [Set.range_eq_empty]
  by_cases h1 : BddAbove (range f)
  · refine (isLUB_csSup (range_nonempty f) h1).unique ?_
    refine (isLUB_congr (hS.continuous_upperBounds hf)).mp (isLUB_ciSup_set ?_ hS.nonempty)
    exact h1.mono (Set.image_subset_range f S)
  · have h2 : ¬ BddAbove (range (fun s : S => f (Subtype.val s))) := by
      intro h
      have := range_comp' f (Subtype.val : S → γ)
      simp_all only [Subtype.range_coe_subtype, setOf_mem_eq]
      have := h.closure.mono (image_closure_subset_closure_image hf)
      simp only [hS.closure_eq, image_univ] at this
      exact h1 this
    simp [csSup_of_not_bddAbove h1, csSup_of_not_bddAbove h2]

requested_change: Replace `exact h1.mono (by grind)` with `exact h1.mono (Set.image_subset_range f S)`.
suggested_fix: Use the standard lemma `Set.image_subset_range` instead of automation; the rest of the proof can stay unchanged.
